html:
The Natchitoches were a Caddo people of the Red River in north-western Louisiana. They gave their name to a confederacy of Caddo villages and to the town of Natchitoches, the oldest European settlement in the lands of the later Louisiana Purchase.

They lived in villages of tall grass houses, grew maize and beans, and were skilled potters. In 1714 the French officer Louis Juchereau de St. Denis founded a trading post beside their village to open trade with Spanish Texas, and the Natchitoches became partners of the French in Louisiana. Disease cut their numbers through the 1700s. The survivors joined other Caddo, and their descendants belong to the Caddo Nation of Oklahoma.
